_why: Read from iter5's own metrics (aes__2026-09-10), per corner: max-slew 532 at max_ss_100C_1v60, 376 nom_ss, 186 min_ss, 9 max_tt, 0 at every ff corner; hold 114/99/66 at the three ss corners and 0 elsewhere. The worst slew pins are antenna-diode nets and flop D pins at 1.37 ns against MAX_TRANSITION_CONSTRAINT 0.75 — OpenLane's default for sky130, while the library's own max_transition is 1.5 ns. The resizer (RSZ_CORNERS defaults to all nine STA corners) found 63 hold endpoints and inserted 63 buffers; signoff then counted 279 at ss, so the repair is seeing a different picture than signoff (estimated vs extracted parasitics), and the post-GRT steps (iter5) did not close the gap. First candidate: the constraint the library actually imposes, one variable. Second: the same plus a hold margin that covers the measured -0.32 ns and no buffer budget cap (default 50% of instances), so the resizer is allowed to reach what signoff measures. iter3's margin 0.3/0.25 was tried at CLOCK_PERIOD 10 while setup was still open; at 12 ns setup has 0 violations to trade against.
_policy_note: OpenLane's own checkers use TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS ['*tt*'] (resolved.json), so by the flow's default policy iter5 would already have passed timing; this pipeline judges all nine corners (score() reads the global counts). Recorded so the stricter gate is a visible choice rather than an accident.
